### ☢️ TAIL RISK #1: Middle East Escalation / Strait of Hormuz Disruption
**Probability Tier: ELEVATED (30–40%)**

This is the most live tail risk on the board. 
The Middle East war has unleashed what S&P Global describes as the largest energy supply shock on record, significantly weakening the 2026 global macro outlook, with higher energy prices pushing inflation materially higher and prompting central banks to pause or reverse easing plans.


**Trigger:** Iranian escalation directly targeting Hormuz shipping lanes, or a broadened conflict drawing in additional state actors — cutting off ~20% of global oil supply.


The Middle East is a crucial node for oil supply; from late 2025 into early 2026, oil already surged over 50% in some measures, taking benchmark prices above the $100 per barrel mark.



Rising oil prices are expected to push headline inflation temporarily toward 4%, eroding real incomes and dampening demand.
 The FOMC's own July minutes flag this directly: 
the staff continued to view the uncertainty around their projection as substantial in light of ongoing geopolitical developments.


**Sectors Hurt Most:** Consumer Discretionary (TSLA, SBUX, MCD), Airlines, Retail (TGT, HD), anything with energy cost pass-through.
